m1_subject: Post-call: SLO gating & connection allowances for StreamX pilot
m1_body:
Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth from the call: 

Summary of StreamX requirements (as captured on the call):
- Target latency: p95 <= 150ms for text-generation prompts <= 256 tokens (in-region).
- Sustained throughput: ~30k tok/s (~250 concurrent generation requests sustained, average 120 tokens/output).
- Burst profile: up to ~750 parallel in 2-minute windows for launches/ingestion spikes.
- Streaming: client expects chunked streaming for progressive responses (they use SSE for partial UI).
- Connection model: they plan to use 40 backend workers each maintaining 16 connections (websocket/long-poll) => ~640 long-lived sockets.

Open items for Redwood to confirm:
1) Can we support the 750 short-term burst while holding p95 target? If not, what are practical burst shapes?
2) How should connection pooling/multiplexing be configured for the StreamX gateway (websockets vs HTTP/2 multiplexing)?
3) Suggested trial quota (baseline + burst) and any credit/discount for pilot.

Proposed next steps: 
- Ben: provide a concrete quota proposal and latency risk notes by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: we'll draft a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) and pilot success criteria and attach.
- Alyssa / Tom: share procurement timelines and any security evidence needed (SOC 2, retention SLA).

Attaching: StreamX-MAP-v1.pdf (working draft), latency-test-samples.json (sample payloads).

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

m2_subject: Re: Post-call: SLO gating & connection allowances for StreamX pilot
m2_body:
Thanks Mina — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 250 concurrent figure is what our orchestration keeps warm for normal traffic; the 750 burst is a combination of short-lived parallelization from our ingestion batch and user-triggered spikes. Bursts will rarely exceed 3 minutes.
- For streaming, we prefer to use WebSocket for multiplexed SSE-style frames today. If Redwood recommends HTTP/2 (server push) we'd consider it, but low overhead per connection is a priority.
- Security: SOC 2 is required; we'll need an evidence pack (attestation + key retention policy) during procurement.

Procurement timeline: tentatively aiming to sign pilot SOW by Nov 25; purchasing contact is procurement@streamx.com.

One ask: if Ben can share an initial quota table (baseline / burst / per-connection QPS) and any recommended connection pooling config, that will help our infra team size the gateway.

Appreciate it — Alyssa

--
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, StreamX
alyssa@streamx.com | +1 503-555-6043
m3_subject: Re: Post-call: SLO gating & connection allowances for StreamX pilot
m3_body:
Alyssa / Mina —

Quick take from infra/quotas: we can support the functional profile but want to propose a controlled pilot shape to validate p95 at scale. Proposed starting quotas for the pilot (30-day):

Baseline (reserved):
- Reserved parallel requests (logical concurrency): 300 parallel generation sessions
- Sustained throughput allowance: 40k tokens/sec aggregate
- Socket allowance: 700 long-lived sockets (websocket/http2)

Burst (elastic):
- Burst pool up to 900 concurrent generation sessions for short windows; bursts > 600 are subject to token-throttling fallback if system memory pressure appears.
- Per-connection QPS soft limit: 120 QPS when multiplexing; 75 QPS per single non-multiplexed websocket connection.

Latency and risk notes:
- With the baseline above we expect p95 <= 150ms for short prompts in-region with standard batching.
- Bursts beyond 600 concurrent will likely increase p95 by 30–80ms depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate; we can mitigate with a transient provisioned capacity bump (we bill for the bump).

Commercials / credits:
- For a 30-day pilot we can offer a 25% consumption credit on token billing up to $15k to offset initial testing costs.
- If StreamX moves to a 12-month reserved commit after pilot, we'll convert to a discounted reserved price (to be negotiated).

Next steps from Redwood: we'll document exact quota names/IDs and config snippets for connection pooling (suggested pool sizes, keepalive, muxing) and send by EOD tomorrow.

Ben

--

m4_body:
Ben — thanks for the clear proposal. A couple of follow-ups from infra/procurement POV:

1) For the burst pool, can you confirm whether bursts are billed at the same per-token rate or if reserved capacity price applies when we trigger a transient bump? We need the cost delta to justify autoscaling triggers.
2) Socket allowance: our gateway currently plans for 800 sockets (40 workers * 20 connections). You listed 700 baseline — can we start the pilot at 800 to avoid rework in our infra?

Procurement note: procurement@streamx.com will need an itemized SOW and the SOC 2 evidence pack to move approvals. Can you route those documents to procurement@streamx.com and CC me?

If you can confirm the billing model for burst vs reserved and the socket change, we can sign off on the MAP and schedule a pilot kickoff for Nov 28.

Thanks — Tom

m5_subject: Re: Post-call: SLO gating & connection allowances for StreamX pilot — next steps
m5_body:
Tom / Alyssa —

Thanks — answering the two asks inline and confirming next steps:

1) Billing model for bursts: bursts drawn from the elastic pool are billed at the usage (per-token) rate during the pilot. If we perform a transient provisioned capacity bump (we allocate additional reserved nodes for a short window), that bump is billed at the reserved rate for the duration of the bump. Ben: I'll let you provide the numeric delta, but the practical implication is: if you expect frequent bursts, we recommend scheduling transient provisioned bumps for the heavy windows to lock-in lower unit cost.

2) Socket baseline: we can start the pilot at 800 sockets as requested. We'll re-label the baseline socket allowance to 800 for the StreamX pilot quota. Note this reduces the elastic socket buffer by 100 in the pilot configuration; we can expand after pilot if needed.

Deliverables we will send today / tomorrow:
- Ben: quota table + config snippets for websocket multiplexing and recommended keepalive values.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence pack routed to procurement@streamx.com.
- Marissa: final MAP with pilot success criteria and test plan.

Proposed kickoff: Nov 28 (pilot window Nov 28–Dec 28). Please confirm by EOD Nov 10 so we can reserve capacity.

I'll attach the finalized MAP once Marissa updates it. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Mina
